# quikleaf

> A standalone, cross-platform desktop markdown editor with rich rendering and LLM chat integration.

## What is quikleaf?

quikleaf is a native desktop application built with Tauri v2 (Rust backend + webview frontend) and powered by quikdown for markdown rendering. It provides:

- Rich markdown editing with live preview
- Built-in LLM chat assistant ("QD"): one sealed chat per document tab (sees and edits only that document), plus a project chat for cross-file work by path; reviewable edits, plan card, per-chat model
- Multiple documents in tabs (Cmd/Ctrl+N, Cmd/Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Tab)
- Writing tools: outline panel, find & replace (case / regex), word count and reading time, focus mode, Export HTML, Print / PDF
- Support for Mermaid diagrams, LaTeX math, GeoJSON maps, 3D STL, CSV tables, Vega charts, ABC music notation, SVG
- Project mode with file tree, the project chat, and a scratchpad + key-value store saved to `quikleaf.prj` along with each project file's chat and pane layout
- Auto-detection of local LLM servers (Ollama, LM Studio, Docker Model Runner)
- Support for OpenAI-compatible APIs (Ollama, LM Studio, Docker Model Runner, OpenRouter, Groq) and Anthropic Claude, with presets in Settings

## Install options

- Pre-built installers (.dmg, .msi/.exe, .deb/.rpm/.AppImage, portable .tar.gz/.zip) from https://github.com/deftio/quikleaf/releases, built automatically for every tagged release from v1.1.0 on.
- npm: `npm install -g quikleaf` (or `npx quikleaf file.md`) — a launcher that downloads the platform binary from the GitHub release of the same version at install time (published via npm trusted publishing / OIDC).
- Build from source: `npm install && npm run setup && npm run tauri:build` (Node 18+, Rust stable, platform webkit deps).
- From the installed macOS app: Help → Install Command Line Tool writes a `quikleaf` shim so `quikleaf file.md` and `quikleaf --project ./dir` work from a terminal.

## Architecture

- Backend: Rust (Tauri v2) — handles file I/O, CLI parsing, LLM API proxying
- Frontend: TypeScript (Vite) — runs in Tauri's webview; UI built with bitwrench.js TACO objects (src/ui/)
- Rendering: quikdown standalone bundle (~8 MB) with all fence renderers included
- LLM: Tool-calling loop; tools are scoped per chat (document chat: 8 document + 2 plan tools, +8 memory/KV for project files; project chat: 5 file, project_search, tabs_list, tab_open, 2 plan, 8 memory/KV); optional review of edits as diff cards (Settings > Agent); a plan card for multi-step work
- Layout: each tab shows [chat | quikdown view | info]; panes and editor mode are remembered per tab

## Key Files

- src-tauri/src/commands/llm.rs — LLM API proxy with streaming
- src-tauri/src/commands/project.rs — Project state, memory, KV, file tools
- src-tauri/src/commands/fs.rs — File I/O commands
- src/ui/theme.ts — bitwrench light/dark themes and app CSS
- src/ui/shell.ts — Title bar, menus, toggle buttons, status bar (TACO)
- src/editor/tabs.ts, src/editor/documents.ts — tab model and session controller
- src/chat/review.ts, src/chat/plan.ts, src/chat/diff.ts — edit review cards, plan card, line diff
- src/ui/findbar.ts, src/ui/outline.ts, src/ui/focus.ts — find & replace, outline panel, focus mode
- src/diag/perf.ts — Timing math and performance-log client
- src-tauri/src/commands/diag.rs — Performance log file + CLI shim installer
- src/chat/chat-ui.ts — Chat pane, scoped tool dispatch, slash commands
- src/chat/session.ts — One chat session per tab (scope, transcript, model, log); quikleaf.prj chat history
- src/ui/panes.ts, src/ui/infopane.ts — Per-tab pane layout and the info pane
- src/chat/providers.ts — LLM provider adapters (OpenAI, Anthropic)
- src/editor/editor.ts — quikdown editor wrapper
- src/settings/settings.ts — LLM configuration UI
- src/project/persist.ts — Debounced quikleaf.prj writer (project_save)
- src/main.ts — Mounts the shell, wires modules, launch mode (file or project)

## LLM Integration Details

The LLM operates on raw markdown only — it never sees or produces HTML. API calls are proxied through the Rust backend to avoid CORS and protect API keys. The tool-calling loop runs at most 10 rounds per turn and can be aborted with the Stop button; there is no per-call timeout.

### Chat scopes and tools

Every tab has its own chat. A document chat is bound to one document: the model sees that document and the conversation only, and its tools can change only that document. Files from unrelated projects open side by side can never reach each other's chats. The project chat (View → Project Chat, project mode) is the only cross-file scope and works on files under the project root by path. The dispatcher enforces the scope: out-of-scope tools return an error.

Document chat: document_read, document_write, document_replace, document_insert, document_undo, document_redo, document_get_selection, document_outline; plan_set, plan_update; memory_* and kv_* only when the document is a file under the project root
Project chat: file_read, file_write, file_list, file_stat, project_search, tabs_list (project files only), tab_open; plan_set, plan_update; memory_read, memory_write, memory_append, memory_clear; kv_get, kv_set, kv_delete, kv_list
Per-chat model: /model <name> (same host/provider as Settings), /model default; also the info pane picker

Edit approval (Settings > Agent): "always" reviews every document and file edit, "files" (default) reviews project file writes only, "never" applies directly. Reviewed edits render as a diff card with Accept/Reject; a rejected tool returns {success:false, rejected:true} and the model is told to ask rather than retry.

## Diagnostics

Timestamps and per-request timing (time to first token, total, ≈tokens, tok/s) show under chat messages; tool calls show their duration. A JSON-lines performance log is written to the OS log dir (macOS: ~/Library/Logs/com.deftio.quikleaf/quikleaf-perf.jsonl) unless disabled in Settings. `/log` shows the path and recent entries. Help → Install Command Line Tool writes a `quikleaf` shim so the macOS app is usable from a terminal.
